title: GST on Ebooks and Online Courses in India (2026)
seoTitle: GST on Ebooks and Online Courses in India (2026)
description: Understand GST questions creators should review before selling ebooks, downloadable resources or online courses in India.
primaryKeyword: GST on ebooks and online courses in India
imageAlt: Educational resources and online course materials

blocks.text: There is no safe one-line GST answer for every ebook, template or course. Treatment can depend on classification, delivery method, customer location, registration status and applicable rate notifications.

Do not assume every digital product has the same classification. A downloadable publication, design file, recorded course, live class and bundle may be treated differently. Separate registration from rate: whether a seller must register and what rate applies to a particular supply are different questions.

For many service providers, the commonly referenced registration threshold is ₹20 lakh, with a lower threshold in certain states, subject to notifications and exceptions. Aggregate turnover is generally computed across India for the same PAN. Specific inter-state and e-commerce provisions may affect the analysis.

A pre-recorded self-paced course may raise different questions from live teaching. Educational exemptions do not automatically apply to every private online course; provider, content and recognition may matter. Cross-border sales can raise place-of-supply, export-of-service, foreign-exchange and documentation questions. A foreign customer alone does not automatically make a transaction an export of services.

Keep product descriptions, customer and location records where relevant, invoices, payment statements, refunds, contracts and delivery evidence. Ask a qualified professional to review classification, registration, rate and invoicing.
Do not assume all ebooks or downloads are exempt; check classification and notifications.
Are recorded and live courses treated the same?
No; state, supply type and exceptions matter.
Does a payment gateway calculate GST on my sales?
No. It may charge GST on its own fees but does not determine your sales-tax liability.
Tax disclaimer: General educational information, not tax, legal or accounting advice. Have a qualified professional review your specific product and sales model.
